title: Search Query Precision and Recall Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI for EE Research
description: Learners calculate precision and recall to two decimal places for three search queries (narrow, broad, and balanced) run on a synthetic corpus of 20 papers with 8 relevant papers, with two attempts per query and a tolerance of 0.01, and then choose the query for a literature survey that cannot afford to miss a relevant paper. Worked TP, FP, and FN counts, the reason for the correct choice, and a score with a mastery statement are shown.

educational.topic: Precision and recall of literature search queries
learningObjectives: Calculate the precision and recall of three search queries run on a corpus of twenty papers with eight known relevant papers
Choose the query that suits a stated purpose, using recall when a missed paper is costly
prerequisites: True positive, false positive, and false negative

accessibility.notes: describe() provides a screen-reader description; all controls are native HTML buttons, checkboxes, text inputs, and a select reachable with the Tab key, and Enter in a value field checks the values. Returned papers are shown with solid borders and the others with dashed borders, relevant papers carry a star glyph, learner marks a check-mark glyph, and correct or incorrect feedback uses check and X glyphs and words as well as color. Colors are blue and brown/orange, which are distinguishable with common color-vision deficiencies.

controls.label: Reveal Relevant Set
controls.purpose: Shown at the start; reveals which papers in the synthetic corpus are relevant (P1 to P8), marked with a star.

controls.label: P1 ... P20
controls.purpose: One checkbox for each paper returned by the current query; the learner marks the relevant returned papers as a counting aid. Not scored.

controls.label: Precision
controls.purpose: The learner types precision as a decimal to two places; correct when within 0.01 of the reference value.

controls.label: Recall
controls.purpose: The learner types recall as a decimal to two places; correct when within 0.01 of the reference value.

controls.label: Check Values
controls.purpose: Checks both values; two attempts per query. A hint follows a first wrong attempt, and the worked counts follow a correct answer or the second attempt.

controls.label: Next Query / Go to Purpose Question
controls.purpose: Shown after a query is scored; moves to the next query, and after query C to the purpose question.

controls.label: Your choice
controls.purpose: Choose Query A, B, or C for the stated purpose.

controls.label: Submit Choice
controls.purpose: Submits the single attempt at the purpose question and shows the answer, the reason, the worked values, and the score.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Worked calculation on concrete result sets with limited attempts and hint-then-reveal feedback, followed by a decision that uses the computed measures
keyQuestions: What fraction of the results are relevant, and what fraction of the relevant papers were found?
You are starting a literature survey and cannot afford to miss any relevant paper. Which query should you run first?
commonMisconceptions: A query that returns many results is a good query
High precision means the search found everything relevant
Precision and recall always move together
assessmentOpportunities: At least 5 of 6 precision and recall values within 0.01 of the reference values, and the purpose-question choice correct, is evidence of mastery
Browsing the corpus and marking papers is exploration and is not evidence
